newsitem.title: INDIA: India CMIE sees 96/97 oilseeds output at 23.4 mt.
newsitem.headline: India CMIE sees 96/97 oilseeds output at 23.4 mt.

text.p: India's oilseeds production in 1996/97 (November-October) is expected to be higher at 23.4 million tonnes compared to 22.6 million in the previous year, the Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy (CMIE) said.

The Bombay-based independent think-tank, in its October review of the Indian economy released on Wednesday, estimated the kharif or winter oilseeds crop at 13.2 million tonnes against 12.8 million in the previous season.
It said harvesting of groundnut, India's most popular oilseed, began in October and would be completed in the current month across the country.
Sowing of the rabi or summer oilseed crop will begin sometime next month and next January.
The federal government has already announced a rise of 30 rupees per quintal (100 kgs) in minimum support prices for rabi oilseeds in a bid to encourage their production.
State-run procurement agencies buy oilseeds if their market prices fall below the minimum support prices.
